title: His Father Took Loans. His Coach Never Charged a Rupee. On Monday, Manav Suthar Broke a 46-Year Record.
excerpt: The 23-year-old left-arm spinner from Sri Ganganagar claimed 6-33 on Test debut, the best figures by an Indian left-arm spinner in a first Test since Dilip Doshi in 1979. His family watched from home — too nervous to stay at the ground.
body:
Jagdish Suthar is a retired Physical Education teacher from Sri Ganganagar, a small city in Rajasthan that sits closer to the Pakistan border than to Jaipur. He had travelled to Mullanpur with his wife and daughter Mansi to watch his son receive an India Test cap on Friday. By Saturday morning, they had left the stadium. They were too nervous to watch.

"Yes, me, my wife and my daughter Mansi had come to watch his debut," Jagdish told PTI. "I can't describe how it felt seeing him get the Test cap yesterday. However today we had come back home as we were all nervous and a bit superstitious watching him live in action from the stadium."

What they missed, watching on television back in Sri Ganganagar, was one of the finest debut performances in Indian cricket history.

## 6-33 in 22 Overs

Manav Suthar, 23, claimed six wickets for 33 runs in 22 overs — including ten maidens — as India bowled out Afghanistan for 152 in their first innings on the third morning of the one-off Test in Mullanpur on Monday. His economy rate of 1.50 was extraordinary. His control was relentless.

Those figures made him only the fifth Indian to take a six-wicket haul on Test debut, joining Narendra Hirwani, Ravichandran Ashwin, Dilip Doshi, and Syed Abid Ali. They were the best by an Indian in a debut Test innings in 38 years — since Hirwani's legendary 8-61 against the West Indies in Chennai in 1988. And they broke Doshi's 46-year-old record for the best bowling figures by an Indian left-arm spinner on debut: Doshi had taken 6-103 against Australia in Chennai in 1979. Suthar took the same number of wickets for 70 fewer runs.

India enforced the follow-on with a 412-run lead. Washington Sundar took 4-36 and Kuldeep Yadav claimed 3-30 as Afghanistan folded for 112 in their second innings. India won by an innings and 300 runs — their biggest Test victory in history.

## The Road from Sri Ganganagar

The story behind the numbers begins in a government school cricket ground on the edge of the Thar Desert. Jagdish, who played right-arm off-spin as a young man, noticed his son naturally bowling left-arm at the age of 10 or 11.

"He was in my school where I was a teacher, so he just kept bowling there. Then he started bowling left-arm," Jagdish recalled to RevSportz. "I saw him and thought it looked good. After that, it all started."

Cricket in Sri Ganganagar meant limited facilities and significant costs for a teacher's family. Reports indicate Jagdish took loans to support his son's training and travel for tournaments. Through it all, one man refused to take a single rupee: Dheeraj Sharma, Manav's childhood coach, who trained him for years without charge.

"It is completely Manav's hard work and the hours that he has put into practice," Jagdish said. "He would leave home for training in the morning and return late in the evening. It is his credit and his childhood coach Dheeraj Sharma to whom we are all indebted. Manav learnt all his cricket under him."

Manav rose through Rajasthan's age-group ranks — Under-14 captain, Under-16, Under-19, Under-23 — before making his first-class debut for Rajasthan in 2022. He accumulated 129 wickets in first-class cricket. He was called up to India's 2023 ODI World Cup preparation camp, where he impressed Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. He was picked by Gujarat Titans for IPL 2026, playing four matches. None of it was guaranteed. All of it was earned.

## "Rajasthan Ka Jadeja"

Indian cricket media had begun calling Suthar "Rajasthan ka Jadeja" — Rajasthan's Jadeja — a comparison to the great all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja. On Monday in Mullanpur, the comparison felt less like aspiration and more like description. Suthar's ability to generate drift, extract sharp turn, and maintain miserly control over long spells is strikingly reminiscent of Jadeja's best days in Test cricket.

Ashwin was among the first to congratulate him. "Manav Suthar. Best wishes for a wonderful career ahead," he wrote on social media — from one spinner who rewrote debut records to another who has just begun.

Sunil Gavaskar, watching from the commentary box, was struck not only by the bowling but by Suthar's composure with the bat. He scored 28 in India's first innings. "What stood out was not just his bowling, but also the confidence he showed with the bat, particularly in the way he used his feet and looked comfortable at the crease," Gavaskar said.

## What Comes Next

Suthar finished the match with 6-33 — his only bowling figures, since India won by an innings and did not need to bowl twice. The challenge now is whether he can replicate this on flatter pitches against stronger batting lineups. Gavaskar noted as much: "A sterner examination awaits on flatter tracks, where success demands greater variation and adaptability from spinners."

India's next assignment is a three-match ODI series against Afghanistan starting June 14, followed by T20Is against Ireland and a full white-ball tour of England. Whether Suthar features in the limited-overs squads remains to be seen. But his Test credentials, established in one devastating morning in Mullanpur, are beyond question.

In Sri Ganganagar, a retired teacher and his wife watched their son's six-wicket haul on television. They had been too superstitious to stay at the ground. They need not have worried.

*The boy from the border town did not need them in the stands. He had brought the whole country to its feet.*
